nuevos.titulo_original: 7 Silent Signs of Pancreatic Cancer
nuevos.descripcion:
Many people don’t know they have pancreatic cancer until it’s too late. The earlier you can detect it, the better the prognosis.

Watch the FULL video here: ▶️ https://youtu.be/o_Uro77TvvQ

🌟 Take Dr. Berg’s New 60-Second Quiz: https://drbrg.co/4khCLkP

Pay attention to these 7 early warning signs: https://drbrg.co/3Uw5Uyk

1. Sudden unexpected weight loss

A problem with the pancreas can affect digestion and appetite, which can cause you to lose weight unexpectedly.

2. Abdominal pain

This is typically dull, persistent pain that can radiate to the left shoulder. Sometimes, it shows up as radiating pain in the belly button that extends into the spine and often feels worse after eating.

3. Jaundice

This is characterized by yellowing of the whites of the eyes and rust-colored urine caused by bile backing up into the blood.

4. Chronic diarrhea

Most pancreatic cancer affects the part of the pancreas that is responsible for digestive enzymes, which can often lead to chronic diarrhea.

5. Diabetes

A tumor in the pancreas can disrupt the cells that produce insulin, contributing to diabetes.

6. Feeling full quickly

Pancreatic cancer can cause you to feel full and bloated, even if you’ve hardly had anything to eat.

7. Persistent fatigue

This can be described as overwhelming, chronic fatigue that doesn’t improve with more sleep.

nuevos.titulo_original: Weird Heart Disease Effect of Cheese
nuevos.descripcion:
Cheese is high in saturated fat, yet it may affect cholesterol differently than butter. One possible explanation is the cheese matrix—the structure of cheese and how its nutrients interact during digestion.

In a randomized trial, full-fat cheese lowered LDL cholesterol more than reduced-fat cheese supplemented with butter, despite similar amounts of saturated fat, protein, and calories.

Another study found that people eating cheese excreted more fat in their stool than those eating butter, suggesting that cheese may reduce fat absorption. Calcium, proteins, and other components of the cheese matrix may help explain this effect. Many variables remain unknown - this is important to acknowledge. 

Results aren’t perfectly consistent, but overall they suggest that a food’s saturated-fat content doesn’t fully predict its cardiovascular effects.

How to Use This: Cheese can fit into a heart-healthy diet, but more isn’t necessarily better. Potential benefits may level off around 50 grams per day.

Viscerální neboli vnitřní tuk nemusí být na první pohled vidět. Přesto jeho nadměrné množství souvisí s vyšším rizikem inzulinové rezistence, diabetu 2. typu, kardiovaskulárních onemocnění a dalších metabolických komplikací.

Dobrá zpráva? Množství viscerálního tuku můžeme významně ovlivnit. Jen možná trochu jinak, než vám tvrdí reklamy na spalovače tuků nebo zázračné diety.

✅ Proč je viscerální tuk rizikovější než běžný podkožní tuk a jak poznat, zda ho nemáte příliš.

✅ Jak bych sestavil praktický plán na redukci břišního tuku.

Muchas personas toman chía en ayunas, en agua con limón, después de dejarla hidratando toda la noche. Es un buen hábito, pero un estudio publicado en 2012 por el equipo de David Nieman, con 62 mujeres después de la menopausia, mostró algo que casi nadie sabe. Por eso buena parte de la chía entera entra y sale del cuerpo sin liberar su aceite. Remojarla forma un gel por fuera, el mucílago, que es una fibra soluble, pero no abre la semilla. Entrainment is one of the most powerful aspects of our biology.

Our circadian rhythm is created within us, but numerous studies show that our health is best when it is entrained to the rising and setting of the sun. That’s not to say you have to wake up at sunrise, but people who try to live nocturnally definitely suffer health consequences and people who match their sleep rhythm even somewhat to the rising and setting of the sun (one form of entrainment), derive many health benefits.

Entrainment works on shorter time scales too. Exercise at roughly the same time for a few days and you’ll notice your energy will increases a few minutes before that typical workout time.

Study or do some reading or some other form of work or learning at roughly the same time or times per day, and you’ll notice that your mental sharpness will start to increase in anticipation of those times.

To be clear, some of this is psychological, but a lot of it is physiological. The neuromodulators, hormones and neurotransmitters that regulate alertness and focus are readily susceptible to entrainment.

And entrainment is a concept that we can leverage. Not to make us rigid, but understanding it can help you make better sense of why you are more energetic and mentally sharp at particular times of day, and it can give you flexibility over what those times are.
